series_items.subject: [RFC PATCH 1/4] block: do not issue background swap bios as root
series_items.patch_summary: This RFC patch proposes to modify the behavior of bio_issue_as_root_blkg() to not issue background swap bios as root, allowing cgroup IO controllers to throttle such I/O. The change is motivated by the fact that some swap writes are best effort and can be throttled without stalling indefinitely on swap writes.

review_comments.author: Christoph Hellwig
review_comments.summary: Questioned whether REQ_BACKGROUND implies that I/O can be throttled, suggesting that the caller should tolerate a failure if it is foreground paging.
review_comments.raw_body:
On Mon, Sep 28, 2026 at 10:18:36AM +0200, Alexandre Ghiti wrote:
> bio_issue_as_root_blkg() issues every REQ_SWAP bio as root, bypassing
> the cgroup IO controllers, because reclaim cannot stall indefinitely on
> swap writes. Some swap writes are not urgent though: zswap writeback is
> best effort.
> 
> Such a bio cannot simply drop REQ_SWAP: dm-crypt and dm-thin rely on it
> for limit_swap_bios, which caps in-flight swap bios to avoid a memory
> deadlock, see commit a666e5c05e7c ("dm: fix deadlock when swapping to
> encrypted device").

Is that true?  REQ_BACKGROUND very much implies the I/O can the throttled
and thus better not be foreground paging, and thus the caller should be
able to tolerate a failure.

series_items.subject: [RFC PATCH 2/4] mm/zswap: turn shrink_memcg_cb()'s argument into a flags word
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the `shrink_memcg_cb()` function in the zswap module to accept a flags word instead of a boolean pointer as an argument. The flags word allows callers to pass additional information, specifically whether the walk stopped at an entry already in the swap cache. This change does not introduce any functional changes but rather provides a more flexible way for callers to interact with the function. The patch defines a new flag `ZSWAP_SHRINK_SWAPCACHE` and updates the function's logic accordingly.

series_items.subject: [RFC PATCH 3/4] mm/zswap: allow writeback to be throttled by the cgroup IO controllers
series_items.patch_summary: This patch allows the cgroup IO controllers to throttle zswap writeback operations by introducing a new 'throttled' flag in the swap_io_ctx structure. When this flag is set, the write operation is issued as background I/O instead of being exempt from cgroup throttling, which avoids priority inversion and ensures that memory reclaim is not stalled for other workloads.

series_items.subject: [RFC PATCH 4/4] mm/zswap: move reclaim-driven writeback to a kworker
series_items.patch_summary: This patch moves the reclaim-driven writeback of zswap to a kworker, improving performance by avoiding stalls in application threads or kswapd. The kworker writes back swap entries in batches of SWAP_CLUSTER_MAX while holding a reference on the memcg, and reports nothing freed until the worker runs. This change is necessary because cgroup IO controllers throttle zswap writeback, causing stalls that were observed in production workloads.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This RFC patch series aims to improve the performance of zswap by making its shrinker writeback work with iocost. The current implementation causes a large production workload to be slower when zswap is enabled, due to two main issues: (1) zswap writeback being charged as debt and causing stalls in application allocations, and (2) throttled writes sleeping in their submitter, which can be an application thread. The patches propose to throttle zswap writeback instead of making it REQ_SWAP, and move the reclaim-driven writeback to a per-lruvec kworker.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH 2/2] btrfs: commit after deleting an unused block group if system space is low

version_history.subject: [PATCH 2/2] btrfs: commit after deleting an unused block group if system space is low

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch addresses a problem where deleting multiple unused block groups in one transaction can fail due to insufficient system space, resulting in an -ENOSPC error. To solve this issue, the patch introduces a mechanism that checks for low system space and commits a single transaction to delete a single block group at a time. This approach allows the system to recover unallocated space and improves the chances of successfully allocating system chunks. The patch modifies the btrfs_delete_unused_bgs function in fs/btrfs/block-group.c to implement this new behavior.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH 1/2] btrfs: allocate additional SYSTEM space earlier

version_history.subject: [PATCH 1/2] btrfs: allocate additional SYSTEM space earlier

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch addresses a performance issue in Btrfs file systems where large block devices can accumulate thousands of system chunks, leading to slow deletion of unused block groups when the file system is filled up and then freed en-masse. The problem arises because the current implementation allocates new system chunks only when the space left is smaller than the reservation for a single chunk tree update. To fix this, the patch introduces a new function `system_space_needed` that estimates the upper bound on bytes needed to modify every leaf in the chunk tree and allocates additional system space earlier, ensuring that all block groups can be deleted in one transaction.

review_comments.author: Filipe Manana
review_comments.summary: Reviewer Filipe Manana questioned the logic of one specific hunk in the patch, pointing out that if left >= bytes is always true at this point because a system chunk has already been allocated when left < bytes.
review_comments.raw_body:
So this hunk I have trouble understanding it, because if left >= bytes
should always be true at this point, as if if left < bytes we have
allocated a system chunk (if we haven't then ret has an error value).

Otherwise it looks good (as well as the second patch).

Thanks.

review_comments.author: Boris Burkov (author)
review_comments.summary: Author acknowledged that the current condition in reserve_chunk_space() can be confusing and proposed to rename system_space_needed() to system_space_target() to better differentiate between the need for a new system chunk and the minimum space required for future allocations.
review_comments.raw_body:
It is a bit confusing and I am not sure how to make it as nice as
possible. So the condition is:

  low = left < bytes || info->total_bytes < system_space_needed(info)
  ...
  if (low) {
  ...
  }

So ret != 0 implies low is true, but not necessarily left < bytes.
Basically the idea is that if the chunk allocation designed to protect
the chunk space in the future fails but we still have enough for right
now (ret && left >= bytes) then we can still add bytes to the block_rsv.

Would it help if I tried to give separate names to the two conditions
and did something like:

needs_space = left < bytes
wants_space = total < system_space_target()
low = needs_space || wants_space

...

if (!ret || !needs_space) {
 ...
}

So rename system_space_needed() to system_space_target() or something
like that, and then differentiate the minimum to add to the block_rsv
more clearly from the desire to add a system chunk? The current
system_space_needed() is kinda misleaded cause with writeback re-cowing,
we might use more than that in a txn anyway so it is not a hard
guarantee.

Thanks for the review,
Boris

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH 0/2] btrfs: ENOSPC fixes for unused block groups

version_history.subject: [PATCH 0/2] btrfs: ENOSPC fixes for unused block groups

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series addresses ENOSPC (no space left on device) errors caused by unused block groups in a Btrfs filesystem. The patches aim to prevent these errors by allocating system chunk space earlier and committing deletions of unused block groups more aggressively when the system is low on space.
